cause_gap: Verified evidence places apple trees in a Novgorod archaeological plot in the second half of the 11th century; that plot was abandoned by the early 13th century. A garden associated with Archbishop Afanasy falls within his 1682–1702 tenure at Kholmogory, but its contents are unspecified; a later journalistic Solovki account describes fruit-growing with heated greenhouses. The verified Arkhangelsk climate table reports a July mean of 16.5°C and record minimum of −45.2°C, but does not state the normals period. This is an editorial climatic indicator for excluding a dedicated fruit-orchard type from the 1230 Lower Dvina starter baseline, not a reconstruction of 1230 climate or proof of biological impossibility.
closure_evidence_or_decision: Reopen only if verified pre-1400 Lower Dvina evidence documents fruit cultivation and gives a period-appropriate cultivation/climate basis strong enough to revise the starter-scope decision.

cause_gap: Verified Lavrova findings place the Palaeozoic base of the lower Dvina below river level at borehole depths of 55–93 m; the oldest Carboniferous horizons are noted below Ust-Pinega, and Palaeozoic rocks are exposed only on tributaries (Ladma, Kekhta, Brusavitsa, Lai) whose distance from the starter nodes is not established. The verified Orlets source says the 1342 fortress was built from nearby limestone, but does not date the start of quarrying. These findings do not support an accessible bedrock quarry in the 1230 Vikhtuy/Zaostrovye starter scope. Regional glacial erratic boulders are documented separately; their occurrence/density at exact starter nodes is not established, so this does not exclude loose-stone gathering.
closure_evidence_or_decision: Reopen if verified site-specific geology identifies accessible quarryable bedrock within the starter scope and dated evidence supports quarrying there by the relevant period. Loose boulder collection requires a distinct type and exact-site evidence.

cause_gap: Verified biogeographic sources place the natural northern limit of the honeybee near 60°N, south of the Lower Dvina start at about 64.5°N. Avdeev describes the range from southern France to Siberia, reaching 60°N, citing Ruttner (1990) and Petrov (1992); Brandorf and Ivoylova separately state the 60°N limit for Russia, to the Urals. Both are secondary statements of the standard range and are not shown to be independent. A verified but unsourced encyclopedic sentence says bee-keeping was important in Novgorod's northeastern dependencies before the 14th century; it names no locality and is not taken as Lower Dvina evidence. This supports excluding wild-hive bortnichestvo from the 1230 starter baseline. It is a range-based scope decision, not proof that imported, managed, or exceptional colonies were physically impossible.
closure_evidence_or_decision: Reopen if a verified pre-1230 source documents locally present wild colonies/borti or a locally applicable bee introduction that changes the natural-range basis. A primary source that localizes the encyclopedic northeastern bee-keeping statement on the Lower Dvina also reopens this row.
